title: Service without reward reaches the Master
subtitle: Raag Gauree
summary: The shabad starts by defining the servant who lives in the Guru's household: obedient, unadvertised, and absorbed in Naam. It comes to a sharp center where selfless service without reward reaches the Lord Himself.
whyItMatters: This one meets the person doing good while keeping one eye on recognition. Lived with faithfully, it purifies service by taking self-display and reward out of the center.
takeaway: Carry this with you: service becomes true when the self stops asking to be seen.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰ ਕੈ ਗ੍ਰਿਹਿ ਸੇਵਕੁ ਜੋ ਰਹੈ ॥
lines.transliteration: gur kai gireh sevak jo rahai ||
lines.translation: That selfless servant, who lives in the Guru's household,

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰ ਕੀ ਆਗਿਆ ਮਨ ਮਹਿ ਸਹੈ ॥
lines.transliteration: gur kee aagiaa man meh sahai ||
lines.translation: is to obey the Guru's Commands with all his mind.

lines.gurmukhi: ਆਪਸ ਕਉ ਕਰਿ ਕਛੁ ਨ ਜਨਾਵੈ ॥
lines.transliteration: aapas kau kar kachh na janaavai ||
lines.translation: He is not to call attention to himself in any way.

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਰਿ ਹਰਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਰਿਦੈ ਸਦ ਧਿਆਵੈ ॥
lines.transliteration: har har naam ridhai sadh dhiaavai ||
lines.translation: He is to meditate constantly within his heart on the Name of the Lord.
One who sells his mind to the True Guru
that humble servant's affairs are resolved.
One who performs selfless service, without thought of reward,
shall attain his Lord and Master.
One whom the Lord Himself blesses with His Grace

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਸੋ ਸੇਵਕੁ ਗੁਰ ਕੀ ਮਤਿ ਲੇਇ ॥੪॥੫॥
lines.transliteration: naanak so sevak gur kee mat lei ||4||5||
lines.translation: O Nanak, is the selfless servant who lives the Guru's wisdom. ||4||5||

structure: First, it begins by describing the servant who lives under the Guru's command rather than personal image.
Then, it sells the mind to the Guru and lets affairs be resolved there instead of in self-importance.
Finally, it ends with selfless service drawing the servant into the Lord and the Guru's teaching.
